name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Agent-generated hypothesis: R382 in the STAT3 DNA-binding domain contacts DNA, and the bulkier tryptophan either removes that contact or sterically clashes with the DNA, lowering DNA affinity and blocking target-gene activation. Loss of DNA binding is the likely basis of loss of function.", "mechanism_class": "nucleic_acid_binding", "supports": ["E4", "E13", "E16", "E5"], "would_refute": "In DNA-bound experimental structures (e.g. 6QHD), the R382 side chain has no atom within about 4 \u00c5 of any DNA atom, and a W382 model placed into that complex shows no steric clash with DNA or the protein core. Equally, an in silico R382W complex with DNA that keeps DNA affinity at wild-type level would refute it.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "E4 is the only record item that describes this exact substitution's functional effect, stating reduced DNA-binding ability in UniProt, and E13 and E16 place residue 382 inside the DNA-binding domain and a DNA-bound structure. E5 says most HIES STAT3 variants act dominant-negatively, which is consistent with a DNA-binding defect. Still missing: any direct DNA-binding measurement for R382W (G1), and a check of whether R382 actually touches DNA in 6QHD (no contact analysis in the record)."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Agent-generated hypothesis: R382W weakens STAT3 homo- or heterodimer contacts. The mutant then either fails to pair with the partner needed for activity (for example EGFR or wild-type STAT3), or pairs with wild-type STAT3 in a non-productive way that sequesters it, which would be dominant-negative.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E5", "E19", "E7", "E21"], "would_refute": "In the AlphaFold DB model and in dimeric or partner-bound experimental structures, R382 lies outside every interface residue set (no atom within about 5 \u00c5 of the other chain or partner), and an R382W model keeps the interface geometry and predicted binding energy within noise of wild type.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "The dominant-negative pattern in E5 and the broad EGFR interaction in E19 make a partner-contact defect plausible. However, E19 has no residue mapping, and E7 places the variant in the DNA-binding domain rather than a dimer interface, so the support is indirect. It ranks below the nucleic_acid_binding hypothesis because E4 and E13 tie the residue directly to DNA binding. Missing: the STAT3 dimer interface residue map and an EGFR interface map (not in the record)."}
